subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should #99449 be resolved by a narrow stale OpenAI route/doctor-owner repair first, by the broader #87957 shared session-state resolver, or by treating explicit `/model openai` sessions as expected and only improving diagnostics?
rationale: Source proves DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the live report mixes Codex hot reload, persisted selected model state, and an explicit `/model openai` clarification, so automation should not choose the permanent session-state contract on its own.

options.title: Fix narrow route drift first
options.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal `openai` doctor ownership while keeping #87957 as the broader resolver tracker.

options.title: Fold entirely into #87957
options.body: Use #87957 as the canonical owner and copy this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload scenario into its acceptance criteria before closing #99449 later.

options.title: Treat explicit OpenAI selection as expected
options.body: If maintainers decide the report is only `/model openai`, keep Codex-for-OpenAI behavior and improve status/doctor messaging instead of changing routing.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal `openai` doctor ownership while keeping #87957 as the broader resolver tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex doctor ownership, and session utility behavior involved in this decision.
